A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 22-page DEX study, including Appendices A–G. Text and visual comparisons establish identical content on pages 2–22; page 1 has only contact and version-header edits.

before.justification: v1 reports original differential-attention analyses and DEX experiments on language modeling, retrieval, in-context learning, and instruction tuning, with additional empirical results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original experimental results in Sections 2 and 4 and Appendices B–E, including benchmark evaluations, ablations, and efficiency measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the identical output-value differential transformation, head-selection strategies, lambda annealing, and trainable parameter groups. Equations 3–5 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Training corpora and task coverage are identical, including the 11 language-modeling benchmarks, multi-needle retrieval, TREC/Banking-77/Clinic-150 in-context learning, and Appendix C's instruction-tuning evaluations.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments, including Table 1's LoRA, PiSSA, FT, GaLore, and APOLLO comparisons and Appendix D's Llama, DIFF, and DEX-S comparisons.

E3.justification: Training and evaluation settings are identical, including Appendix F's one-epoch adaptation with 32k-token contexts and Section 4.2's 20 retrieval samples per depth/context-length combination. No protocols are added or revised.

E4.justification: The attention diagnostics, head-selection and lambda ablations, training-data sensitivity, redundancy analyses, and qualitative examples in Sections 2 and 4.4 and Appendix B are unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical, including Appendix E's throughput averages over 30 batches after five warm-up batches. Run-count, seed, and uncertainty-reporting practices are not revised.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings match. For example, DEX's Llama-3B average remains 64.2 in Table 1, and its average in Table 7's instruction-tuned block remains 63.0.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations and derivations are identical, including Equations 1–6 and Appendix F.3's pseudoinverse and optimization-based effective-attention approximations. No assumptions or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: Both retain the same three mechanistic claims—negative-attention expressivity, reduced head redundancy, and improved learning dynamics—and the same claim of efficient DEX adaptation using less than 0.01% of pretraining data.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including the model/data dependence of the DIFF analysis, the absence of DEX testing above 8B parameters in Section 5, and approximation caveats in Appendix F.3.

D1.justification: Appendices E–F retain identical hardware, corpus composition, hyperparameters, model configurations, and implementation details. Technical and data-resource link destinations are unchanged.

R1.justification: All 92 reference entries and Appendix A's related-work discussion are identical, including positioning relative to DIFF, DINT, negative-attention methods, and attention-head redundancy research.

P1.justification: Two authors' TwelveLabs email addresses are replaced with Gmail addresses, and the arXiv stamp changes from v1/22 May 2025 to v2/4 July 2025. Scientific prose and document organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The replacement emails slightly respace the first-page author block, and the marginal arXiv stamp changes. All figures, tables, captions, and layouts on pages 2–22 are visually identical.

improvement.justification: v2 updates contact information and version labeling with slight first-page respacing. The scientific content, supporting evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information are unchanged, establishing no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
